summary: Game world models have made rapid progress toward real-time interactive generation. Yet action control is still predominantly implemented as feature conditioning, leaving the model to learn from training data how each action should move the visual world.
takeaways: Yet action control is still predominantly implemented as feature conditioning, leaving the model to learn from training data how each action should move the visual world.
As a result, tokens corresponding to the same world location retain the same positional address across time.
This formulation is poorly matched to a broad class of planar-camera worlds, such as top-down and isometric games.
